body.x: Gary Shapiro, the President and CEO of Consumer Electronics Association(CEA), spoke about CES 2015 in an exclusive interview with AVING News. Below is the interview script.
Hello, this is Ashley Gamin Kim from Aving News Corporations. And, I'm here with Mr. Gary Shapiro. Hello. He is the CEO of the Consumer Electronics Association.
Ashley Kim: So, how much you do think things have changed this year in CES compared to last year?

Gary Shapiro: Well, the CES is definitely bigger by every measure. More car companies, more companies with the 3D printing technology, also with robotics as well as wireless health products. Certainly, it's grown in many other ways as well. 3D printing is very very big and drones, the UAV, the unmanned aerial vehicles. It’s very cool and it is growing very very rapidly.
K: And the driverless car technologies with the sensors?

S: Yeah, so It’s only driverless cars the but all the things that lead up to all the safety technology, collision avoiding system, products which look at you to make sure you are awake, paying attention to the road, not diverting for more than a couple of seconds, also the safety technologies are coming very quickly.
K: Were you at the Mr. Koenig's analysis marketing presentation?
K: He was talking about the developing market such as China. What do you think about that?

S: Well, certainly the U.S. only has 5 percent of the world's population. And china is, although the birth rate has definitely dramatically slowed, it is the largest country in the world (population). So we view that it is a very big market, and that's why we are having a show there in May, in Shanghai. We'll have a CES Asia.
K: I've noticed that lots of Korean companies don't usually get involved in CES, so would you give advice to Korean companies to get involved in CES and CEA?

S: Well, two of the most important exhibitors here are LG and Samsung. They not only have a range of the technology and a large exhibit but it is beautiful and such a great presentation and a marketing message, and they've grown with CES, and they contributed a part of their growth to being a CES, which is terrific.But if a company want to do well, they have to establish themselves a brand. And brands are created by five senses of experiences like this one. And at a trade show, where you are forming an impression of a company, and it’s the company and its people whether or not you can do business and trust them. So, if Korean companies want to grow, they have to be involved with CES or other trade shows or events where they get to know people and people can trust them.

K: Well, thank you so much for your feedback, and this is the tenth year that Aving is covering CES so we just wanted to tell you know that we are so dedicated to your show it's an amazing show, every year trade grows and I really appreciate what you did here.
S: Thank you so much. We appreciate you covering us.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
